findings.reason: a done-when whose negative control names no site cannot be executed as written, so the site must be pinned before dispatch or the control phrased against a site the node is granted.
findings.text: the negative control reads "with the named site dropping the queued fields again" and the done-when requires the node to "show that at base the output carries no `queued` object, as observed, and name the site that drops it", yet §23 also says the site is unsettled; a control must mutate a specific site, so under SPEC `exact` the builder cannot write the control until the site is found, and cannot apply it at all if the site lies outside the declared write paths

findings.reason: a node confined to a module that already behaves correctly will find no defect to fix and no way to reproduce the cited answer, so it stops as a blocker; naming the candidate site (or granting its path) is what makes the node buildable.
findings.text: §23 says the hold came from the router-slot allowance in `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py` "which may not reach that branch", but that hold is a `LaneHeld` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1184`), `LaneHeld` is a subclass of `LanePaused` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:1181`), and both `LaneHeld` raise-sites attach the queued record (`held.queued = …` at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1161` and `:264`), so it does reach the `except LanePaused` branch and does set `report["queued"]`; the branch at `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2043` and `_discard_composed_plan_review` already preserve that key and the top-level `run_id`, so the router-slot allowance is not the dropping site and the module §23 names as its only product write path already emits the object the deliverable asks for, leaving the observed loss (no `queued`, no `run_id`) to a site outside the granted scope

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py` and commit `47fadfcc8` all resolve; `_dispatch_composed_review` is at `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1774`, the cited `the lane's router grants … extra workers` string at `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:1236`, and the cited test path is a new file.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the base-arm precondition and the negative control both rest on a site the plan has not located, while the declared write paths cover only the module that already behaves correctly.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate arm, the base arm and the control are logged "under the run directory", a durable path a later reader can open.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `queued`, `queued.run_id` and the test filename `tests/test_a_held_review_says_it_is_queued.py` name the mechanism, with no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the plan's own candidate site is contradicted by the cited code, and the deliverable names no site the mechanism must change while the write fence excludes every other candidate.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §23 carries one deliverable: a composed review the lane holds reports the queued request on the report and on the `crew review` output.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §23 declares no depends-on/informs and needs none: it shares `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py` only with §9, §10 and §15, each carrying `status: done`, so no ordering is implied and no relationship points at the wrong node.
